basics.name: namePrefix
basics.label: Name prefix
basics.toolTip: Prefix for the export storage account. A random suffix gets appended.

options.text: The exports are created on your MCA billing profile, which this deployment can't grant access to. Before deploying, you need a user-assigned managed identity holding Billing account contributor on the billing account (or Billing profile contributor on the profile). The commands under 'Create the export identity' below set one up. The deployment checks this access first and stops within a few minutes, with nothing else created, if it's missing.

elements.name: billingProfileId
elements.label: Billing profile ID
elements.toolTip: MCA billing profile ID. az billing profile list --account-name <billing account id>

elements.name: exportIdentity
elements.label: Export managed identity
elements.toolTip: User-assigned managed identity holding Billing account contributor on the billing account (or Billing profile contributor on the profile). See 'Create the export identity' below if you don't have one.

options.text: A Billing account owner runs these in Azure Cloud Shell. They create the identity in its own resource group (separate from this deployment, so it can be done first) and grant it Billing account contributor on every billing account the person running it can see. Replace <site-name>, run it, then reopen this form and pick the identity above.

elements.name: identitySetupCommand
elements.label: Commands
elements.defaultValue:
# Run in Azure Cloud Shell (Bash) as a Billing account owner.
# Creates the export identity and grants it Billing account contributor on
# every billing account you can see, which covers all their billing profiles.
NAME='<site-name>-umi'
RG='<site-name>-umi-rg'
LOCATION='eastus2'

az group create -n "$RG" -l "$LOCATION" -o none
az identity create -g "$RG" -n "$NAME" -l "$LOCATION" -o none
PRINCIPAL=$(az identity show -g "$RG" -n "$NAME" --query principalId -o tsv)
TENANT=$(az account show --query tenantId -o tsv)

# new identities take a moment to show up in Entra
sleep 30

for ACCT in $(az rest --method get --url "https://management.azure.com/providers/Microsoft.Billing/billingAccounts?api-version=2024-04-01" --query "value[].name" -o tsv); do
  echo "Granting Billing account contributor on $ACCT"
  az rest --method post \
    --url "https://management.azure.com/providers/Microsoft.Billing/billingAccounts/$ACCT/createBillingRoleAssignment?api-version=2024-04-01" \
    --body "{\"principalId\":\"$PRINCIPAL\",\"principalTenantId\":\"$TENANT\",\"roleDefinitionId\":\"/providers/Microsoft.Billing/billingAccounts/$ACCT/billingRoleDefinitions/50000000-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-100000000001\"}" \
    -o none && echo "  granted" || echo "  not granted - see the error above"
done

echo "Pick this identity in the deployment form: $NAME"

elements.name: exportPrefix
elements.label: Export name prefix
elements.toolTip: Stuck on the front of each export name. Leave blank to reuse the name prefix.

elements.name: exportFormat
elements.label: Export format
elements.toolTip: Parquet is smaller and faster to query. Csv is easier to eyeball.

elements.name: enablePrivateEndpoint
elements.label: Create a private endpoint for the export storage
elements.toolTip: Also flips the storage firewall to Deny by default. The exports themselves still arrive over the public endpoint via the AzureServices bypass - this endpoint is for whoever reads the data.

toolTip.virtualNetwork: Create a new VNet or pick one that already exists.
toolTip.subnets: Subnet the private endpoint NIC lands in.

elements.name: privateDnsZoneMode
elements.label: Private DNS zone
elements.toolTip: A VNet can only be linked to one privatelink.blob.core.windows.net zone. If the VNet you picked already has one, use it instead of creating a second.

elements.name: existingPrivateDnsZoneId
elements.label: Existing private DNS zone resource ID
elements.toolTip: Full resource ID of the existing privatelink.blob.core.windows.net zone.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be the full resource ID of a privatelink.blob.core.windows.net zone.

options.text: Using an existing subnet: whoever runs this deployment needs join permission on it (Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action), and the subnet must allow private endpoints.

elements.name: deployDataFactory
elements.label: Deploy the Data Factory mover
elements.toolTip: Untick to stand up the cost management exports only.

elements.name: siteName
elements.label: Site name (destination container)
elements.toolTip: Root container on the customer storage account the exports get sent to, e.g. contoso-adf-focus. Also used to name the Data Factory resources.

constraints.validationMessage: 3-63 chars, lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens. Must start and end with a letter or number.

elements.name: customerStorageAccount
elements.label: Customer storage account name
elements.toolTip: Destination account the export folders get mirrored into.

elements.name: customerToken
elements.toolTip: Account-level SAS for the customer storage account. Needs rwdlac on the blob service.

elements.name: timeZone
elements.label: Time zone
elements.toolTip: Windows time zone ID the triggers and the pipeline date maths run in.

elements.name: monthlyDayOfMonth
elements.label: Monthly run day
elements.toolTip: Day of the month the monthly trigger fires.

elements.name: catchupCutoffDay
elements.label: Catch-up cutoff day
elements.toolTip: N in (today - N). With N=5, runs on the 1st to the 5th still mirror last month's folder.

options.text: ARM always creates Data Factory triggers stopped. After the deployment finishes, run the startTriggersCommand from the outputs to start them.
